row.team_price_text: Starts at $9 per employee per month
row.evidence: Namely's developer docs describe only an Okta SCIM integration that uses "Namely as a master for your user profiles"; Okta can create users in Namely with only first name, last name and primary email, and Namely's SSO page says it "does not support account provisioning for IdPs".
row.notes: Namely is an HRIS, so its SCIM endpoint (https://{company}.namely.com/api/scim/v2) mainly feeds the IdP: Okta imports users and groups from Namely. Going the other way, Okta can create users (first/last name, primary email) and update only the work email; Namely documents no deactivation or deletion from the IdP. JumpCloud's own docs describe a JumpCloud-to-Namely SCIM sync with provision, update and deprovision, which Namely does not document. Which Namely packages include SCIM, the API or SSO is not published: NamelyNow starts at $9 per employee per month and other packages are quote-based. JumpCloud states SSO needs a 'Namely single sign-on (SSO) enabled subscription'. The developer docs at developers.namely.com are JS-rendered (Stoplight); quotes were read through the Stoplight node API. Row idp.jumpcloud changed from via_generic to native: JumpCloud's own catalogue app provisions over Namely's SCIM endpoint. Status stays partial under the post-pilot rules: no plan gate is published, and Namely documents no deactivation or deletion from the IdP (lifecycle gap), even though two IdPs can reach the endpoint.

plans.name: NamelyNow
plans.price_text: Starts at $9 per employee per month

auth.token_source: Okta 'Configure API Integration' redirects to Namely to sign in (OAuth); JumpCloud's docs use a Namely Personal Access Token instead

custom.how: Custom Namely profile fields via external namespace urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:custom:2.0:User (names as shown at /api/scim/v2/Users.json)

limitations.text: Namely documents SCIM only as an Okta integration where Namely is the profile master; IdP-to-Namely provisioning is limited to creating users with first name, last name and primary email.
Only the work email can be updated via the PUT endpoint; usernames should be email and cannot be updated from Okta.
Employees are created and deactivated in Okta from their Namely start and departure dates (HR-driven), not deprovisioned in Namely by the IdP.
Groups flow one way, Namely => Okta (Groups.json endpoint).
Namely's SSO page states Namely does not support account provisioning for IdPs.

endpoints.purpose: Get a list of profiles at your company

rate_limits.text: 100 requests per minute to GET /profiles (HTTP 406 when exceeded); other endpoints not throttled

limitations.text: API access depends on permissions; the API menu may be hidden until granted by the client success manager or a Namely admin.
Groups and teams are read-only in the API (view only).

fallbacks.other_sync: Namely is itself the HR system of record: the Okta integration uses Namely as profile master (HR-driven provisioning into the IdP)

conflicts.text: Namely's SSO page says Namely does not support account provisioning for IdPs, while its Okta SCIM docs list 'Create User (Okta => Namely)' and the fields Okta can send when it creates a user.

open_questions: Which Namely packages include SSO, SCIM or API access is not published (the package comparison on the pricing page is image-based and has no SSO/SCIM rows). JumpCloud says SSO needs an 'SSO enabled subscription'.
Whether an IdP can deactivate or delete a Namely user over SCIM is not documented by Namely (JumpCloud claims deprovisioning works).
SCIM ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, filtering, pagination, PATCH and rate limits are undocumented.
No audit-log API or user-event webhooks found; deactivation via the REST API (e.g. a user_status field on PUT /profiles/{id}) is not confirmed from the pages reviewed.
Namely developer docs at developers.namely.com are JS-rendered; content was read via Stoplight's public node API (stoplight.io), cited directly.
OneLogin connector page could not be loaded (bot protection); namely.com/clients/onelogin is a customer story, not an integration page. No Google Workspace catalogue entry found.
JumpCloud notes its Namely import-only integration will be deprecated by end of 2026.
